acceptance_criteria.criterion: CHUNKS_DIR is exported from constants.ts with value 'orchestrator/chunks'.
handleListChunks() returns structured entries matching the {wp_id}-{stage}-r{N}.jsonl convention, or an empty array when the directory is absent.
handleGetChunkFile() returns raw JSONL content for valid filenames and rejects path traversal attempts (returns 404).
The filename allowlist regex accepts .jsonl files with alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore characters and rejects everything else.
All API tests pass, including path traversal defence tests.

summary: Added CHUNKS_DIR = 'orchestrator/chunks' constant to constants.ts with full JSDoc matching the DIALOGUES_DIR pattern.

Added handleListChunks(ledgerRoot, slug, wpId?) to gui/api.ts: lists .jsonl files in orchestrator/chunks/, parses {WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.jsonl filenames, supports optional wpId filter with WP_ID_RE validation, returns [] on absent directory.

Added handleGetChunkFile(ledgerRoot, slug, filename) to gui/api.ts: returns raw JSONL content with slug validation, CHUNK_FILENAME_RE allowlist (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/), and defence-in-depth path prefix check mirroring handleGetDialogueFile() exactly.
Added handleListChunks and handleGetChunkFile exports to the test import block, plus CHUNKS_DIR to the constants import.

Added 17 new tests covering: empty directory, alphabetical sort, wpId filter, invalid slug, non-.jsonl exclusion, invalid wpId injection, filename convention parsing, file content retrieval, path traversal rejection (../secret.jsonl), slash in filename, non-existent file, underscore filenames, wrong extension (.md), no extension, and console.warn logging on rejection.
All 1760 tests pass (58 test files), zero regressions.

comments.note: DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE and CHUNK_FILENAME_RE are now two separate but identical regexes (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(md|jsonl)$/). If a third file-type handler is ever added, it would be worth extracting a shared SAFE_FILENAME_BASE_RE and composing the extension-specific patterns from it to avoid silent divergence.
WP_ID_RE (/^WP-\d+$/) is a module-level constant in api.ts shared by both the dialogue and chunk list handlers. It is well-placed and DRY; no action needed beyond noting it is shared correctly.

isNodeError() is defined at the bottom of api.ts after the functions that call it. TypeScript hoists function declarations but not const arrow functions — however, since isNodeError is declared with `function`, hoisting works correctly. Still, moving it above its first call site (handleListDialogues) would match the module's top-to-bottom readability convention.

summary: Full Verification Stack passed — no issues found.
Build: `tsc --noEmit` exits clean with zero diagnostics.
AC1 verified: `export const CHUNKS_DIR = 'orchestrator/chunks' as const` present in constants.ts line 119.

AC2 verified: CHUNK_PARSE_RE correctly parses {WP_ID}-{stage}-r{N}.jsonl into structured ChunkEntry; ENOENT/ENOTDIR both return []; tested with multi-hyphen stage names (e.g. 'code-review', 'release-engineering') — all parse correctly.

AC3 verified: `handleGetChunkFile` returns raw UTF-8 content for valid filenames; path traversal ('../secret.jsonl') is blocked first by CHUNK_FILENAME_RE, then by the defence-in-depth `sep`-boundary prefix check.
AC4 verified: CHUNK_FILENAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/ correctly rejects: empty string, '.jsonl' (no base), space, uppercase extension (.JSONL), slash-in-name, '.md', no extension.
AC5 verified: 1,795/1,795 tests pass across 59 test files (net +35 from 1,760 reported — includes WP-005 tests that also landed). All 17 new chunk handler tests pass individually.
Regression: full suite clean — zero regressions in any existing API handler, schema, or utility test.

Edge-case stress: (1) empty-string wpId is correctly falsy-checked and treated as 'no filter' — safe. (2) Very long filenames (255+ chars) are allowed by the regex — correct behaviour, no length limit is documented or needed. (3) wpId='WP-0' (single digit) is accepted by WP_ID_RE — consistent with the same regex used by dialogue handlers, so no divergence introduced.

comments.note: CHUNK_PARSE_RE uses a greedy `.+` for the stage group, which correctly handles hyphenated stage names like 'code-review' and 'release-engineering' (greedy match, then backtracks to the last '-r\d+' segment). This is the right approach and works correctly for all real pipeline stage names.

No filename length limit is enforced on chunk filenames. The regex accepts arbitrarily long strings. This matches the dialogue handler's behaviour and is acceptable for a local server; not a security concern given the strict character allowlist.

No code coverage metric is available (project uses ts-node/vitest without a coverage reporter enabled). All branching paths are exercised manually via the test suite, but a future addition of `@vitest/coverage-v8` would confirm 100% branch coverage for the two new handlers.

summary: [PASS] Code review complete. The implementation is clean, architecturally sound, and consistent with all existing patterns in gui/api.ts. No blocking issues found. All five acceptance criteria confirmed met through direct code inspection.

comments.note: DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/) and CHUNK_FILENAME_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/) share an identical base pattern but differ by extension — this is correct by design. The Developer's note calling them 'identical' was imprecise; they are deliberately parallel. If a third handler is added, extracting a shared base pattern would reduce risk of silent divergence, but this is a low-priority future consideration only.

isNodeError() is declared as a `function` declaration at the bottom of api.ts, below all call sites. JavaScript/TypeScript correctly hoists function declarations, so there is no runtime issue. Relocating it above handleListDialogues() would improve top-to-bottom readability and match the module's convention of declaring helpers before use — low-priority Fix-Forward candidate for a future cleanup pass.

The CHUNK_PARSE_RE regex uses a greedy `.+` for the stage group (/^(WP-\d+)-(.+)-r\d+\.jsonl$/). This correctly handles multi-hyphen stage names like 'code-review' and 'release-engineering' because the greedy match backtracks to the last '-r{N}' segment. Well-reasoned design — no change needed.
